title: rate-limit-heatmap-exports-wireframe-notes
body:
Purpose
---
Working notes for a console UX that combines a high-level heatmap of request intensity with per-key and per-route breakdowns, plus CSV/JSON export and sample-request playback. Focus: make it trivial for platform owners and app teams to spot bursty keys, attribute costs to routes, and take corrective actions (throttle, exception, quota change) without jumping between pages. This is a working doc — rough wireframes, questions, and a prioritized backlog.

Goals (product + UX)
- Surface problem keys quickly: identify top offending API keys or routes by token volume and by rate violations.
- Make root cause triage fast: be able to see sample requests, latency/p50/p95, model used, and matching quota rules in-line.
- Support ops workflows: one-click export (CSV/JSON), replay a sampled request to reproduce, and create follow-up Jira ticket.
- Prevent noise: allow configurable aggregation windows and sampling to keep UI responsive.

Audience
- SRE/Platform engineers monitoring tenant load and incidents.
- Customer success/solutions engineers doing cost root-cause.
- Product owners of integrators who need usage visibility.

Primary concepts to show in UI (wireframe components)
1) Top bar filters (global):
   - Time range selector (last 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, custom)
   - Granularity toggle (1m, 5m, 1h)
   - Model filter (all / by model family)
   - Route type filter (generate, embeddings, chat, rerank)
   - Key filter (search by key id, key label, team tag)

2) Left rail: quick-scan KPIs (small cards)
   - Active keys (count) | Keys over quota (count) | Requests/min peak | Avg token cost per 1k requests
   - SLA violations (count) | Errors (%) last 24h

3) Main canvas split: Heatmap (top) + Detail table (bottom)

Heatmap (visual):
   - X axis = time buckets, Y axis = top N keys (configurable, default 25)
   - Color intensity = normalized token volume (or request count toggle)
   - Hover cell -> tooltip showing exact token count, requests, avg latency, top route in that bucket
   - Click cell -> open right-side inspector for that key/time slice (sample, rules, actions)
   - Heatmap mode toggle: show by tokens | show by violations | show by cost estimate

Detail table (below heatmap):
   Columns: Key id / Label | Total tokens | Requests | Violations | Avg latency p50/p95 | Top route | Model | Action buttons
   - Sortable and column-level filters
   - Row expansion reveals a small timeline sparkline, last 5 sample requests (truncated) with timestamps, and a link to full request playback in a modal

Right-side inspector (drawer)
   - Context for selected Key + Time slice: top routes with % split, quota rule matched, enforcement history (timeline), cost estimate for slice, and a list of sample requests with a "replay" action (redact sensitive content by default).
   - Buttons: Create exception (temporary quota increase), Create quota rule, Create Jira ticket, Export timeframe (CSV/JSON), Add note (internal audit trail)

Export & offline workflows
- Export options: current view -> CSV or JSON; include metadata header (filters applied, time range, aggregation).
- Sampling for exports: default to sampling 1% of requests when export size > 10k rows; give preview of sample size before export.
- Pre-built pivot export: per-key x route matrix with token counts and cost estimates.

Backlog / Implementation tasks (prioritized)
1) MVP: Heatmap + detail table + basic exports (CSV), left-rail KPIs, filters. 
2) Follow-up: Right-side inspector with sample playback and create-exception flow. 
3) Integrations: Jira button that pre-fills issue template; Slack alert links that deep-link to heatmap view.
4) Performance: server-side rollups + pre-aggregated queries to keep heatmap interactive for large orgs.
5) Advanced: cost-estimation model per model/quantization profile; percentiles of token-length distribution per key.

Wireframe notes (visual annotations)
- Heatmap row labels should show key label + short team tag; use subtle color palette (for accessibility use >=4.5 contrast for labels).
- Add small badge for keys in "dedicated" tier vs hosted; allow filter for "dedicated only".
- When a key is suspected of abuse (spike + many routes), row turns amber and a persistent "Investigate" CTA appears.
- For mobile / narrow widths: collapse heatmap to a stacked list of sparklines and an inline mini-heat view per key.

Edge cases and UX decisions to resolve
- How to handle multi-tenant keys (some customers use a single key across many internal apps)? UX: allow tag-based grouping and opaque "owner" field editable by Solutions/CS.
- Rate-limited events: show both enforcement attempts and successful enforcement; enforcement count should not be conflated with request count.
- Sensitive content in sample requests: default redact; provide role-based unredact (requires audit log).
- Long-tailed keys: keys with low sustained usage but occasional huge spikes should be searchable but not dominate heatmap — consider top-N by peak vs top-N by total volume toggle.

Data model / backend notes for BE collaboration
- Required API: GET /analytics/keys?range=&granularity=&filters= -> returns time buckets for top keys + overall aggregates. Must support pagination and top-N parameters.
- Need an endpoint for sampled request fetch: GET /analytics/request-samples?key=&from=&to=&limit=5.
- Export service: server-side streaming CSV generation with preflight that returns estimated row-count and sample percent recommended.
- Pre-aggregation pipeline: hourly rollups per key x route to support fast 7d views.

Open questions (to discuss in grooming)
- Q1: Default top-N = 25? For large enterprise probably 50. Tradeoff: rendering performance vs discoverability.
- Q2: Should exports include raw request bodies (redacted) or only metadata? Security and compliance teams likely prefer metadata-only by default.
- Q3: Do we offer saved views/alerts tied to a key? Requires backend storage and UI for managing saved monitors.

Acceptance criteria (MVP heatmap + table)
- Heatmap loads < 2s for 24h range with top-25 keys for orgs with up to 1M daily requests (with pre-agg).
- Export CSV completes for up to 50k rows via streaming, with sampling applied past threshold.
- In-table action "Investigate" opens inspector with at least 3 sample requests and matching quota rules.
- Role-based redaction applied to sample contents and unredact audit logs created.

UX copy and microcopy examples
- Heatmap tooltip: "12:35 — key: abc-123 — 4,200 tokens (avg latency 420ms) — top route: /v1/chat"
- Export button: "Export view (CSV/JSON) — includes filters and aggregation metadata"
- Investigate CTA: "Open inspector — sample requests & enforcement history"

Metrics & monitoring for product team post-launch
- Adoption: number of distinct orgs using heatmap > 3x/week
- Time-to-investigate: avg time from spike detection (alert) to first investigator action in UI
- Export usage: number of CSV exports per org per month
- False-positive alert rate for spike detection rules (tune thresholds)

Notes / Todo list (short)
- [ ] Finalize top-N default after data-based experiment (Noah)
- [ ] Backend contract draft for analytics endpoints (Priya)
- [ ] Security review for sample playback and export (Liam)
- [ ] Quick prototype in FigJam with two heatmap color modes (Sofia)
- [ ] Add link to billing data for cost-per-token estimation (product ops)

References and related docs
- See product backlog epic: JIRA-ENG-2417 (heatmap analytics)
- Existing quota UI patterns: /product/console-and-rollouts/api-credential-usage-cards-ux-proposals-and-backlog
- Slack thread: #rate-limits-ux-thread for early feedback

Bottom line
This doc sketches a pragmatic starting place: an operations-first heatmap that surfaces per-key and per-route signal, plus a set of actionable controls. Next step: sync with BE to lock the analytics API, then quick FigJam prototype and a 1-week data experiment to validate top-N defaults and sampling heuristics.
